about: How DBaba reasons about a query, in our own words: read it as stages (output, tables, links, row filters, totals, group filters, windows, final cut), state what one result row stands for, then check each stage against the fundamentals below. Every finding of the SQL checker names the fundamental it breaks. Learned from the official manuals first; practice problems only point at what to check.

checklist.en: What must each result row show?
checklist.hi: Har result row mein kya dikhna chahiye?
Ye values kin tables mein hain?

checklist.en: How are the tables linked, and is each link one-to-one or one-to-many?
checklist.hi: Tables kaise jude hain, aur har link ek-se-ek hai ya ek-se-kai?

checklist.en: Which raw rows are kept (WHERE), and does a filter on an outer-joined table undo the outer join?
checklist.hi: Kaunsi rows rakhi jaati hain (WHERE), aur kya outer-join wali table ka filter outer join ko khatam karta hai?

checklist.en: What is totalled (COUNT/SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX), and at which level?
checklist.hi: Kya total hota hai (COUNT/SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX), aur kis level pe?

checklist.en: What does one result row stand for (the grain)?
checklist.hi: Ek result row kis cheez ki hai (grain)?

checklist.en: Is a condition on a total in HAVING, not WHERE?
checklist.hi: Total wali condition HAVING mein hai, WHERE mein nahi?

checklist.en: Should it be split into stages (subqueries / CTEs), each at one grain?
checklist.hi: Kya ise stages mein todna chahiye (subquery / CTE), har stage ek grain pe?

checklist.en: Is ranking, a running total or a previous-row comparison needed (window functions)?
checklist.hi: Ranking, running total ya pichhli row se compare chahiye (window functions)?

checklist.en: Which rows survive at the end (HAVING, rank filter, LIMIT), and is the order deterministic?
checklist.hi: Aakhir mein kaunsi rows bachti hain (HAVING, rank filter, LIMIT), aur order pakka hai?

checklist.en: Which filters and joins need an index, and does a function on a column stop the index?
checklist.hi: Kin filters aur joins ko index chahiye, aur kya column pe function index rok deta hai?

checklist.en: For each subquery: where does it stand (one value, a set, EXISTS), and which names tie it to the outer row?
checklist.hi: Har subquery ke liye: wo kahan khadi hai (ek value, set, EXISTS), aur kaunse naam use bahar ki row se jodte hain?

grain.title_en: Grain: what one row stands for
grain.title_hi: Grain: ek row kis cheez ki hai
grain.rule_en: Every stage of a query has a grain (one row per order, per customer, per category). Totals, comparisons and ranks are only right when they are taken at the grain the question asks for; mixing two grains in one step is the most common silent mistake.
grain.rule_hi: Query ke har stage ka ek grain hota hai (har order, har customer, har category ki ek row). Total, compare aur rank tabhi sahi hain jab sawaal wale grain pe liye jaayein; ek step mein do grain milana sabse aam chhupi galti hai.

cardinality.title_hi: Cardinality: ek-se-kai link rows ko guna karte hain
cardinality.rule_en: Joining a table with many rows per key repeats the other side once per match. Two such joins on the same parent multiply each other, so totals of either side grow; total each child at its own grain first, then join the totals.
cardinality.rule_hi: Kai rows wali table join karne se doosri taraf har match pe dohraati hai. Ek parent pe do aise join ek doosre ko guna karte hain; pehle har child ka total uske apne grain pe nikaalo, phir join karo.

outer_join.title_en: Outer joins keep unmatched rows, with NULLs
outer_join.title_hi: Outer join bina match wali rows rakhta hai, NULL ke saath
outer_join.rule_en: A LEFT JOIN keeps every left row; where nothing matches, the right-side columns are NULL. A WHERE condition on those columns removes the unmatched rows again (put it in ON instead), and COUNT(*) counts the unmatched row as 1 (count a right-side column instead).
outer_join.rule_hi: LEFT JOIN har left row rakhta hai; match na ho to right ke columns NULL hote hain. Un columns pe WHERE condition bina match wali rows hata deti hai (ON mein likho), aur COUNT(*) unhe 1 ginta hai (right ka column gino).

null_logic.rule_en: Any comparison with NULL is unknown, not true or false: = NULL never matches (use IS NULL), and NOT IN over a list that contains a NULL matches nothing (use NOT EXISTS). Arithmetic with NULL is NULL (COALESCE(x, 0) when missing means zero), and where NULLs sort differs: first in ASC on MySQL/MariaDB, first in DESC on PostgreSQL.
null_logic.rule_hi: NULL se har comparison anjaan hota hai, na true na false: = NULL kabhi match nahi karta (IS NULL likho), aur NULL wali list pe NOT IN kuch match nahi karta (NOT EXISTS likho). NULL ke saath hisaab NULL hota hai (khaali ka matlab zero ho to COALESCE(x, 0)), aur sort mein NULL MySQL/MariaDB pe ASC mein pehle, PostgreSQL pe DESC mein pehle aate hain.

filter_level.title_en: WHERE filters rows, HAVING filters groups
filter_level.title_hi: WHERE rows filter karta hai, HAVING groups
filter_level.rule_en: WHERE runs on single rows before any totals exist, so it can't use SUM()/COUNT() or names made in SELECT. A condition on a total belongs in HAVING after GROUP BY.
filter_level.rule_hi: WHERE totals banne se pehle ek-ek row pe chalta hai, isliye SUM()/COUNT() ya SELECT ke naam use nahi kar sakta. Total wali condition GROUP BY ke baad HAVING mein.

subquery_shape.title_en: A subquery is one value or a set
subquery_shape.title_hi: Subquery ek value hai ya ek set
subquery_shape.rule_en: Where a subquery stands decides how much it may return. After = < > or in the SELECT list it must give one row and one column; after IN / NOT IN / ANY / ALL one column and any number of rows; after EXISTS only whether there is at least one row matters, so what it selects doesn't matter, and an aggregate without GROUP BY always gives exactly one row (EXISTS (SELECT COUNT(*) ...) is always true). LIMIT without ORDER BY inside it keeps whichever row came first. A subquery is evaluated against the data as it was when the statement started, and MySQL won't let it read the table an UPDATE/DELETE is changing unless it is wrapped as a derived table; MySQL and MariaDB also refuse LIMIT inside IN and a subquery in FROM without a name.
subquery_shape.rule_hi: Subquery kahan khadi hai, wahi tay karta hai wo kitna de sakti hai. = < > ke baad ya SELECT list mein ek row aur ek column; IN / NOT IN / ANY / ALL ke baad ek column aur kitni bhi rows; EXISTS ke baad sirf ye ki koi row hai ya nahi, isliye wo kya select karti hai farak nahi padta, aur GROUP BY ke bina aggregate hamesha ek row deta hai (EXISTS (SELECT COUNT(*) ...) hamesha true). Andar ORDER BY ke bina LIMIT jo row pehle mili wahi rakhta hai. MySQL UPDATE/DELETE ki apni table ko subquery mein tabhi padhne deta hai jab use derived table mein lapeta jaaye; MySQL/MariaDB IN ke andar LIMIT aur bina naam ki FROM subquery bhi nahi maante.

values_types.title_en: Values have types: text in quotes, dates in quotes
values_types.title_hi: Values ke type hote hain: text aur date quotes mein
values_types.rule_en: A word without quotes is a column name and a date without quotes is arithmetic (2024-01-01 is 2022). Each side of a condition must be a whole comparison: status = 'a' OR 'b' compares nothing on the OR side; write IN ('a', 'b'). BETWEEN needs the smaller value first. Operators depend on the type and the engine: + adds numbers (text joins with CONCAT; || joins text only on PostgreSQL), integer / integer drops the fraction on PostgreSQL, in LIKE % and _ are wildcards, and double quotes mean a name on PostgreSQL.
values_types.rule_hi: Bina quotes ka shabd column ka naam hai aur bina quotes ki date hisaab hai (2024-01-01 = 2022). OR ke dono taraf poora comparison chahiye: IN ('a', 'b') likho. BETWEEN mein chhoti value pehle. Operator type aur database pe nirbhar hain: + number jodta hai (text CONCAT se; || sirf PostgreSQL pe text jodta hai), PostgreSQL pe integer / integer decimal kaat deta hai, LIKE mein % aur _ wildcard hain, aur PostgreSQL pe double quotes naam hote hain.

names_scope.title_hi: Naam ek scope ke hote hain
names_scope.rule_en: Once a table has an alias, only the alias works; a column with no table in front is ambiguous when two joined tables have it; a name made in SELECT exists only for ORDER BY (and HAVING in MySQL), never for WHERE.
names_scope.rule_hi: Table ko alias dene ke baad sirf alias chalta hai; do tables mein same column ho to bina table ke naam ambiguous hai; SELECT mein banaya naam WHERE mein nahi chalta.

ranking.rule_en: LIMIT cuts the whole result once; 'top N per group' needs a window function partitioned by the group. ROW_NUMBER() gives tied rows different numbers, RANK() gives them the same rank with gaps, DENSE_RANK() without gaps. ORDER BY gives one exact order only when its last column is unique; otherwise ties (and a LIMIT without ORDER BY) return rows in no promised order.
ranking.rule_hi: LIMIT poore result ko ek baar kaat-ta hai; 'har group ke top N' ke liye group se PARTITION wala window function chahiye. ROW_NUMBER() barabar rows ko alag number deta hai, RANK() same rank (gaps ke saath), DENSE_RANK() bina gaps. ORDER BY tabhi pakka kram deta hai jab aakhri column unique ho; warna barabari (aur bina ORDER BY ka LIMIT) koi tay kram nahi deta.

time_ranges.rule_en: '2026-01-31' on a column with time means midnight at the start of that day. Write ranges as >= start AND < next period start: right for DATE and DATETIME alike, and a plain column comparison can still use an index (a function like YEAR(col) can't).
time_ranges.rule_hi: Time wale column pe '2026-01-31' ka matlab us din ki shuruaat (00:00). Range >= start AND < agla period likho: DATE aur DATETIME dono pe sahi, aur index bhi chalta hai (YEAR(col) jaisa function nahi).

changes_safety.title_en: Changing data: which rows, how often, what value, which column
changes_safety.title_hi: Data badalna: kaunsi rows, kitni baar, kya value, kaunsa column
changes_safety.rule_en: A change touches exactly the rows its WHERE and joins let through, so run the same FROM and WHERE as a SELECT first. Every joined table must be tied to the target row, or every target row passes; PostgreSQL's FROM in an UPDATE is a separate list, so naming the target table there again adds an unlinked copy. Each target row is changed at most once per statement, so a row with several matching child rows gets one of them (total the children first). SET col = (SELECT ...) gives NULL where the subquery finds nothing. INSERT ... SELECT fills the column list by position, never by name. Deleting duplicates needs a rule for which copy stays (t1.id > t2.id). In SET, assignments are separated by commas (AND makes one boolean expression). Change very large sets in batches.
changes_safety.rule_hi: Change wahi rows chhoota hai jo uska WHERE aur joins dete hain, isliye pehle wahi FROM aur WHERE SELECT mein chalao. Har joined table target row se judi honi chahiye, warna har row badalti hai; PostgreSQL ke UPDATE ka FROM alag list hai, wahan target table dobara likhna ek bina-judi copy hai. Har target row ek statement mein ek hi baar badalti hai, isliye kai child rows mein se ek hi lagti hai (pehle total banao). SET col = (SELECT ...) match na mile to NULL deta hai. INSERT ... SELECT position se bharta hai, naam se nahi. Duplicate hatane mein batao kaunsi copy rahe (t1.id > t2.id). SET mein comma, AND nahi. Badi rows batches mein.

precedence.title_en: Conditions combine in a fixed order: NOT, then AND, then OR
precedence.title_hi: Conditions ek tay kram mein judti hain: NOT, phir AND, phir OR
precedence.rule_en: AND binds tighter than OR, like multiplication before addition, so a OR b AND c is a OR (b AND c). Bracket every OR that is one choice among several.
precedence.rule_hi: AND OR se pehle lagta hai, jaise jod se pehle guna, isliye a OR b AND c ka matlab a OR (b AND c). Jo OR ek hi chunav hai uspe bracket lagao.

join_condition.title_en: A join condition must connect the right rows
join_condition.title_hi: Join condition sahi rows ko jodni chahiye
join_condition.rule_en: Every joined table needs a condition that ties it to a table already in the query, usually child.foreign_key = parent.primary_key. A join with no condition, or with one that mentions only one of the two tables, pairs every row with every row (a cartesian product). Comparing two primary keys (o.id = c.id), a key the wrong way round, or a column that isn't unique on the parent side (a name) pairs rows that don't belong together. NATURAL JOIN and USING pick the columns by name, so a shared column like id or created_at joins things that aren't related. In a self join the same row also meets itself, and every pair appears twice unless one side is kept smaller (a.id < b.id).
join_condition.rule_hi: Har judi table ko ek condition chahiye jo use pehle se maujood table se jode, aam taur pe child.foreign_key = parent.primary_key. Bina condition ka join, ya aisi condition jo sirf ek table ka naam leti hai, har row ko har row se jodta hai (cartesian product). Do primary keys ko milana (o.id = c.id), ulti key, ya parent ki aisi column jo unique nahi (naam), galat rows jodti hai. NATURAL JOIN aur USING naam se column chunte hain, isliye id ya created_at jaisi common column bekaar rishta bana deti hai. Self join mein row khud se bhi milti hai, aur har jodi do baar aati hai jab tak ek taraf chhoti na rakho (a.id < b.id).

engine_syntax.title_en: Each database has its own syntax beyond standard SQL
engine_syntax.title_hi: Har database ka standard SQL ke alawa apna syntax hai
engine_syntax.rule_en: SQL is the shared language, but each database adds its own words: MySQL/MariaDB have backtick names, LIMIT offset,count, IFNULL, GROUP_CONCAT, DATE_FORMAT; PostgreSQL has :: casts, ILIKE, DISTINCT ON, NULLS FIRST/LAST, string_agg; SQL Server has TOP n, [brackets], GETDATE(). A database refuses another one's words, so the answer depends on which database runs the query: name it, or DBaba reads it from the query.
engine_syntax.rule_hi: SQL sabki common language hai, par har database apne shabd jodta hai: MySQL/MariaDB mein backtick naam, LIMIT offset,count, IFNULL, GROUP_CONCAT; PostgreSQL mein :: cast, ILIKE, DISTINCT ON, NULLS FIRST/LAST; SQL Server mein TOP n, [brackets], GETDATE(). Ek database doosre ke shabd mana kar deta hai, isliye jawab is baat pe tika hai ki query kaunsa database chalayega.

aggregation.title_en: A total sees only the rows and values that reach it
aggregation.title_hi: Total sirf unhi rows aur values ko dekhta hai jo us tak pahunchti hain
aggregation.rule_en: An aggregate works on the rows left after WHERE and the joins, and of those only on the values that are not NULL; COUNT(*) is the one that counts rows. So COUNT(x) counts filled values, not true ones (a 0 or a false is counted); SUM and AVG skip NULLs, so AVG is the average of the rows that have a value, and SUM of no rows or of only NULLs is NULL, not 0; DISTINCT inside a total works on values, so equal amounts of different rows count once. Totals are made once per group: a total can't hold another total at the same level (do it in two stages), and in a grouped query a window function sees one row per group, so its argument must itself be a total. An average of per-group averages weighs every group the same, and a share is only right when its total covers the same rows as its part.
aggregation.rule_hi: Aggregate WHERE aur joins ke baad bachi rows par chalta hai, aur unme bhi sirf un values par jo NULL nahi; sirf COUNT(*) rows ginta hai. Isliye COUNT(x) bhari values ginta hai, true wali nahi (0 ya false bhi gina jaata hai); SUM aur AVG NULL chhod dete hain, to AVG sirf value wali rows ka average hai, aur khaali ya sirf-NULL ka SUM NULL hai, 0 nahi; total ke andar DISTINCT values par chalta hai, to alag rows ki barabar raqam ek baar gini jaati hai. Total har group ka ek baar banta hai: total ke andar total ek hi level par nahi chalta (do stage mein karo), aur grouped query mein window har group ki ek row dekhta hai, to uska argument bhi total hona chahiye. Group averages ka average har group ko barabar wazan deta hai, aur share tabhi sahi hai jab total un hi rows ka ho jinka hissa hai.

correlation.title_en: A subquery reads its own FROM first
correlation.title_hi: Subquery pehle apna FROM padhti hai
correlation.rule_en: A name inside a subquery is looked up in the subquery's own FROM first and only then in the query around it. A subquery is tied to the outer row (correlated) only through a name that belongs to the outer query; without one it gives the same answer for every row. So when the subquery reads the same table again, orders.customer_id inside it means the inner orders (x = x, always true) unless the inner copy gets a name of its own; a column of the outer row in the subquery's SELECT list just repeats the row's own value; and IN (SELECT MAX(y) ... GROUP BY g) gives values without saying which group they belong to, so a row matches any group's maximum, not its own. Compare the pair ((g, y) IN (SELECT g, MAX(y) ...)) or correlate on g.
correlation.rule_hi: Subquery ke andar naam pehle uske apne FROM mein dhoondha jaata hai, phir bahar wali query mein. Subquery bahar ki row se tabhi judti hai (correlated) jab usme bahar wali query ka koi naam ho; warna har row ka ek hi jawab. Isliye wahi table dobara padhne par andar orders.customer_id andar wali orders hai (x = x, hamesha true) jab tak andar wali copy ko apna naam na do; SELECT list mein bahar ki row ka column bas usi row ki value dohraata hai; aur IN (SELECT MAX(y) ... GROUP BY g) values deta hai par ye nahi batata kis group ki, isliye row kisi bhi group ke max se match ho jaati hai. Jodi compare karo ((g, y) IN (SELECT g, MAX(y) ...)) ya g par correlate karo.

routine_flow.title_en: A routine must end, answer, and not feed itself
routine_flow.title_hi: Routine ko khatam hona, jawab dena, aur khud ko na chalana zaroori hai
routine_flow.rule_en: A loop ends only when its condition reads something the body changes, or when it reaches LEAVE / EXIT / RETURN. A function must reach a RETURN on every path; a PostgreSQL trigger function returns the row to save (RETURN NEW), and NULL from a BEFORE row trigger means skip the row. A trigger must not run a statement on its own table: MySQL/MariaDB refuse it (1442), PostgreSQL fires it again until the stack runs out. To change the row being saved, change NEW in a BEFORE trigger; in an AFTER trigger the row is already saved.
routine_flow.rule_hi: Loop tabhi rukta hai jab condition kuch aisa padhe jo body badalti hai, ya LEAVE / EXIT / RETURN aaye. Function ko har raaste pe RETURN chahiye; PostgreSQL trigger function save hone wali row lautata hai (RETURN NEW), BEFORE row trigger se NULL ka matlab row chhodo. Trigger apni hi table pe statement na chalaye: MySQL/MariaDB mana (1442), PostgreSQL baar baar chalata hai. Row badalni hai to BEFORE trigger mein NEW badlo; AFTER mein row save ho chuki hoti hai.
